title: A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) of a finitely generated torsion-free group G_proj and a projection e in its reduced group C*-algebra with 0 < tau(e) < 1/2, which disproves the Kadison-Kaplansky conjecture. The first lesson reduces the theorem to a self-adjoint matrix over the group ring of a torsion-free group with a separated spectral band of unnormalized trace in (0, 1/2), by compression after a free product; the second proves the spectral and trace tools. Lessons 3 to 7 build an infinite layered graph, the tower, from streams, slots and gated permutations, prove the uniform gap of its mean incidences and the expansion of the realized incidences, and prune it so that long paths are recovered from their words and short cycles disappear. Lessons 8 to 10 define the group by the closed walks of a voltage cover of the tower and prove that its components embed in the Cayley graph, that triangles in the coned Cayley graph are uniformly thin, that each copy has one finite ball containing its overlaps with earlier copies, that the remaining edges form a forest, and that the group is torsion-free. Lessons 11 to 14 build the voltage group, a torsion-free nilpotent central product of affine groups detecting short words, its Schwartz idempotents and lattice projections, and a finite magnetic factor that makes the weighted trace small at both ends of the central parameter. Lessons 15 to 17 realize the model operator on the cover with one random draw per edge, finitely many matrix weights and large girth; the last lesson transfers the separated band to the Cayley graph and bounds its trace.
prerequisites: programme course Foundations of von Neumann algebras: lessons C*-algebras, continuous functional calculus, automatic continuity and positive cones (Theorems 3.2 and 5.1, Corollary 5.4) and The spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators (Proposition 5.2)

programme course A projection of irrational trace and the Baum-Connes conjecture (irrational-trace-and-baum-connes): lessons Traces of projections and the Baum-Connes conjecture (Lemma 1.1, Section 3) and Graphical presentations and coned diagrams (Section 3)
programme course Index theory of elliptic operators: lesson Hermite functions, tempered distributions and the Schwartz kernel theorem (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 2.2, Corollary 4.2)
programme course The Bass trace conjecture for group rings (bass-trace-conjecture): lesson Idempotents and integral traces (Theorem 2.1), for context

programme course Van Kampen diagrams (van-kampen-diagrams): lessons Plane maps (Propositions 1.2, 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3) and Van Kampen's lemma (Definition 1.1, Theorems 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1), which prove the statements (VK) and (MAP)

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison-Kaplansky projection conjecture' (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026; local clone openai-math-20261006, TeX of all sections and the compiled text) was read in full on 15 and 16 Oct 2026, and every step was checked while the lessons were written: scalar compression and torsion in free products; the identity trace, the compression of a separated band and the contour estimate; streams, slots, slot evaluations and the coefficient lemma; gated permutation rules, the edge equations and the folded alphabet; the conditional Fourier estimate, causality and the mean gap below 0.8; the mean cut, the tail of a cut, the asymmetric local lemma and the passage from cuts to the incidence norm; recovery of prefixes and the three kinds of deletions; voltage covers, the reduction rules, short arcs and embeddings; short chain fillings and thin triangles with D_0 = 10^6, avoidance, overlap balls, cycle coordinates, the residual forest and the incidence count; stabilizers and the acyclic cone complex; the rank bound, pivot words and the matrix detector; the affine group, its grading, the deck group and the fiber representations; Schwartz idempotents, weighted Riemann sums and discrete twisted projections; the magnetic factor, absorption, layer windows and the weighted trace; the model band, finite tests and empirical averages; templates, masks, finite lists, the subgroup factorization and the edge distribution; the Schwartz-Zippel bound, girth, walks without singleton edges, centered moments and the simultaneous choice; the cover projection, localization of trace, trimming, the forest norm, the spectral band and the trace bound. No error affecting a statement was found. One intermediate inequality in the proof of Lemma 9.4 omits a factor of at most 2: the number of index sequences, the sum over a <= k of M^a a^(2k), is at most 2 M^k k^(2k), not M^k k^(2k); the conclusion is unaffected, and the course carries the factor. Changes of form in the course: Lemma 10.1 is proved with the constant a + 12 epsilon, which the manuscript's proof also gives; the conventions for left and right translations and the conjugation by inversion are made explicit wherever fibers and identity traces are used; the measurability of the cover projection is derived from continuous functional calculus on fields; the separate accuracies of the template approximation, the lists and the rounding are fixed in one order; the compactness argument of Section 9.9 is written out. Later literature, read on 15 and 16 Oct 2026 in arXiv searches (all:'Kadison-Kaplansky'; all:'idempotent conjecture'; abstracts with 'torsion-free', 'projection' and 'C*-algebra'; all:'voltage' AND all:'small cancellation'; all:'Kaplansky' AND all:'projection'): no preprint after 23 Sep 2026 proves, disputes or extends the theorem; S. V. Ivanov, arXiv:2610.17662 (13 Oct 2026), extends OpenAI's zero-divisor counterexample to every odd characteristic and is cited in the first lesson as context. Check program plan/checks_20261016/kk_check.py, run kk_check_run_20261016a.txt (15 Oct 2026, 23:03 UTC): 23 of 23 checks pass. Exact: the constant c_a of scalar compression; cardinalities, stream lengths, the two cutoff forms, the degrees D_ik and d|A_i| = D_ik|B_k| for 54,090 adjacent pairs (l = 1..30); the families and the alphabet count; the deletion bound and the threshold l >= 4 of the short-cycle count; the recovery length in the tower proposition; the constants L*, C_*, C_bullet and the ball bound; the matrix detector on 300 random words with integer matrices, and its degree bound symbolically for m = 4 with fixed factors; the affine group for m = 3 symbolically (associativity, inverse, cocycle identity, dilations, Haar Jacobians); torsion-freeness of 200 integer elements; the finite magnetic representation R(g)R(h) = e(-c(g,h)/q)R(gh) for 230 random integer pairs and five (m, q); the parameter inequalities of the weighted trace bound and of (3.1) of the lesson on masks for the minimal admissible E_0, A_*, kappa, for m up to 10^60; boxes in F with exact boundary counts; the walk counts of the moment lemma; the Schwartz-Zippel bound by exhaustive evaluation of 131 polynomials over F_5, F_7, F_11; walks without singleton edges on 12 random graphs (44,248 walks); the union bounds of the girth and moment arguments with the actual constants; the constants of the last lesson. Numerical: the Gaussian Schwartz idempotent for m = 2 (twisted convolution by quadrature, error 4e-14); near-idempotents and the bounds of Proposition 3.1 of the lesson on Schwartz idempotents; the smooth layer windows; the model band on five finite two-layer models; the finite norm test in Z; Fourier tails of narrow masks by FFT; Lemmas 3.1 and 4.2 of the lesson on separated bands on 40 random examples; the forest norm bound on 30 random trees; the localization of Proposition 3.1 of the last lesson on 10 layered models.

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course: (LUCK) Lück's theorem on the traces of assembly classes (Lück, The relation between the Baum-Connes conjecture and the trace conjecture, Invent. Math. 149 (2002), Theorem 0.3, on the author's university page), used only for the remarks on the Baum-Connes conjecture in the first lesson. Van Kampen diagrams (VK) and plane maps (MAP), stated in Section 3 of the lesson Graphical presentations and coned diagrams of the course irrational-trace-and-baum-connes and used in the lessons Voltage covers and embedded copies and Thin triangles, overlap balls and the residual forest, are proved in the course Van Kampen diagrams (van-kampen-diagrams); Theorem 1.1 uses no named statement of this course.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
